title: CHAPTER SIXTEEN. On faith: definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Paul calls it ye faith belonging toward ye elect; Hebrews 11:1 describes it as ye hypostasis belonging toward things hoped for, ye conviction belonging toward things not seen. — Thus far ye external means belonging toward our salvation; there follows ye internal, namely FAITH: a fiduciary assent and acknowledgment belonging toward ye truth which stands as according toward godliness, unto hope belonging toward eternal life which God who does not lie promised before ye ages and manifested in His times (Tit. 1:1-3). — CHAPTER SIXTEEN. On faith.
pass_b_english: Thus far the external means of our salvation; there follows the internal, namely FAITH: a fiduciary assent and acknowledgment of the truth which is according to godliness, unto hope of eternal life which God who does not lie promised before the ages and manifested in His times (Tit. 1:1-3).
Paul calls it the faith of the elect; Hebrews 11:1 describes it as the hypostasis of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM SEXTUM, De fide. Atque haec de mediis salutis nostrae externis: sequitur internum, nempe FIDES, quae est assensus fiducialis atque agnitio veritatis quae est secundum pietatem, in spem vitae aeternae quam promisit qui non mentitur Deus ante tempora saecularia, et manifestavit temporibus suis (Tit. 1:1-3). Ordo postulat ut hic agamus de fide (cf. lib. IV cap.7). Hanc fidem appellat electorum, tum quia electis communis est, tum quia est de communi salute (Jude 3). Huc referri potest Apostolica descriptio Heb. 11:1: Fides est hypostasis eorum quae sperantur, elenchus rerum quae non videntur.
